title: Complex sentences
subtitle: Inversion, cleft sentences, and so / such / too / enough

theory.title: Inversions with negative adverbial words and phrases

blocks.text: When a negative or restrictive adverbial starts the sentence, we invert the auxiliary (or **do/does/did**) and the subject. This is typical of formal written English.

rows.example: **Hardly** had the new law been introduced **when** the mistake was realised.
**Scarcely** had I opened the front door **when** I heard a noise from the kitchen.
**Barely** had we solved one problem **when** another one arose.
**No sooner** had the alarm gone off **than** the police arrived.
**Only** in an emergency should you dial 999.
**Only after** I had checked that the burglars had left did I call the police.
**Only when** we agree what measures are needed will we be able to solve the problem.
**Not until** the next election will we know how the public feel about this news.
**At no point** did I realise that he was the Prime Minister.
**In no way** does this decision represent a change in government policy.
**Little** did Ralph know that the burglar was still inside his house.
**Never** have I heard such a ridiculous suggestion!
**Not** one vote did the proposal receive.
**Not only** has this government failed **but it has also** stolen ideas from other parties.
**On no account** should you try to tackle a burglar yourself.
**Rarely** do the newspapers present a balanced view of current events.
**Seldom** do people leaving prison stay out of trouble.
**Under no circumstances** will we accept an increase in working hours.

blocks.text: With **not until** and **only** (when / after), invert the verb and subject in the **main clause**, not in the clause that immediately follows **not until / only when**.
blocks.note: **Not until / Only when** this government realises what a mistake it is making **will things change**.

theory.title: Inversions with adverbial expressions of place

blocks.text: After **here, there** and some adverbial or participle phrases of place, we can invert a verb of movement or position and the subject. This is common in literary or journalistic style.

rows.example: **Here comes** the Minister now.
**There stood** the next king of England.

**At the top of society** are the aristocracy. · **Beside the Town Hall** stood the public library. · **In this prison** are housed some of the most dangerous criminals. · **On the corner of the street** sat a homeless man.
**Running down the road** was a young man with a woman's handbag under his arm.

rows.use: short answers with so, neither and nor
rows.example: 'I voted for Smith.' '**So did I.**' · 'I don't believe a word this government says.' '**Neither / Nor do I.**'

rows.use: after as, than, so and such
rows.example: I am very worried about bullying in the school, **as are** a lot of the parents. · The police in this area make more arrests **than do** officers in other parts of the country. · **So rare** is burglary here that many people don't bother to lock their doors. · **Such public interest was there** in the story that it was on the front pages of the newspapers.

**Were** the Foreign Secretary to resign, it would cause serious problems for the Prime Minister. · **Should** the Foreign Secretary resign, it would cause serious problems for the Prime Minister. · **Had I known** about the crime problem, I would never have moved here.

blocks.text: Cleft sentences split one idea into two clauses so that we can emphasise a particular part of the sentence.

rows.example: **All that** Keith wanted was to get his money back. · To get his money back was **all that** Keith wanted.
**It was Carol who/that** called the police.
**The first thing** is to check to see what's missing. · To check to see what's missing **is the first thing**.

rows.use: the day/year etc when/that · the day/year etc on/in/at which
rows.example: **The year** when this government came to power was 2006. · 2006 was **the year when** this government came to power. · 2006 was **the year in which** this government came to power.
**The person who** stole the money was Thomas. · Thomas was **the person who** stole the money.
**The place where** the Queen stays in Scotland is Balmoral Castle. · Balmoral Castle is **the place where** the Queen stays in Scotland.
**The reason (why)** I joined this political party was to make a difference. · To make a difference was **the reason (why)** I joined this political party.
**The thing that** annoys me is the boss's attitude. · The boss's attitude is **the thing that** annoys me.
**What** annoys me is the boss's attitude. · The boss's attitude is **what** annoys me.
**What** Churchill **did** was bring people together.
**What happened was** that a witness saw the man leave the house.

blocks.text: With **It is/was …** in cleft sentences, there are two possibilities when the subject is a pronoun. They differ in formality.
blocks.note: **It was I who** stole the money. (formal) · **It was me that** stole the money. (informal)

rows.example: It all happened **so quickly** that I didn't have time to see the man's face. · This problem has gone on for **so long** that I don't think they'll ever find a solution. · It was **so terrible a crime** that the judge sentenced him to life in prison. · There is **so much crime** around here **that** I'm thinking of moving.

This problem has gone on for **such a long time** that I don't think they'll ever find a solution. · It was **such a terrible crime** that the judge sentenced him to life in prison. · There is **such a lot of crime** around here **that** I'm thinking of moving.

I had **too little time** to get a good look at his face. · This problem seems to be **too difficult** for them to solve. · The police responded **too slowly** to have any chance of catching the burglar.
There just aren't **enough** police officers on the streets. · The police weren't **quick enough** to catch the burglar. · The police didn't respond **quickly enough** to catch the burglar.

blocks.text: **So** and **such** can also be used in various ways without a **that** clause.
blocks.note: There's **so much** crime around here these days. · Politics is **so boring**! · You're **such a bully**!

blocks.text: We only use **too** to describe something that is more than necessary and which has a negative effect. It is not the same as **very, really, extremely**, etc.

blocks.correct: This problem seems too difficult for them to solve.
blocks.incorrect: This problem seems too difficult for them to solve it.

items: It is not necessary to add an extra object in sentences such as **too + adjective + for + object + to-infinitive**.
**Enough** usually comes before nouns and after adjectives and adverbs.

exercises.title: A · Tick or rewrite
exercises.instruction: If the phrase in bold is correct, write a tick (✓). If it is incorrect, rewrite the inverted phrase correctly.

items.prompt: **Hardly I had sat down** when the doorbell rang.
acceptedAnswers: Hardly had I sat down when

items.prompt: **Scarcely had Julian finished** writing when the teacher told the students to put their pens down.
We had barely set off on our journey when **the kids started** asking when we would get there.
**No sooner the government changes** the tax laws than businesses find a way around them.
acceptedAnswers: No sooner does the government change
No sooner has the government changed

items.prompt: **Scarcely they had finished** painting the house when it started to rain.
**Hardly the new computer system had been installed** when it started to go wrong.
acceptedAnswers: Hardly had the new computer system been installed

items.prompt: It's true that **no sooner we had started** eating than we realised we had forgotten the potatoes.
Barely had the politician started to speak when **began the crowd** to boo.
**Hardly the new park was finished** when vandals destroyed the flowerbeds.
acceptedAnswers: Hardly had the new park been finished
Hardly was the new park finished

items.prompt: **Scarcely Keith had arrived** in Argentina when he was arrested.

exercises.title: C · Verb form after inversion
exercises.instruction: Complete using the words in brackets with the verb in the correct form. Write the inverted (or non-inverted) verb phrase only.

items.prompt: Not until the area is made safe ___ . (construction / can continue)
In no way ___ how strongly we felt about the situation. (the announcement / affect)
Seldom ___ a vintage car in quite such good condition these days. (you / see)
Not only ___ my birthday, but he also forgot our wedding anniversary. (Jerry / forget)
At no time ___ my opinion on the subject. (I / ask)
Only when ___ the ticket again did I realise that I had won first prize! (I / check)
Little ___ that I had a big surprise planned for her. (Caroline / realise)
Under no circumstances ___ a contract you haven't read thoroughly. (you / should sign)
At no stage ___ likely that Wilkinson would win the championship. (it / appear)
Only if the weather is clear ___ to launch. (the space shuttle / will allow)
acceptedAnswers: will the space shuttle be allowed

exercises.title: E · Circle the correct phrase
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct phrase. If both are possible, choose the option that includes both.

items.prompt: Dave doesn't really trust Ian, and I have to say that neither ___.
Such a valuable painting ___ that the public are not allowed to get close to it.
So ___ watch TV while we ate, we moved the television onto the balcony.
My dad's never been abroad, and nor ___.
options: my mum has / has my mum

items.prompt: Such ___ in the wedding that there were over a dozen photographers.
options: the media interest was / was the media interest

items.prompt: It's been a hard season for the team, as ___.
options: last season was / was last season

items.prompt: Russia is a country with vast natural resources, and so ___.
We in this country spend more per person on fuel than ___.
options: the French do / do the French
acceptedAnswers: the French do / do the French

items.prompt: The Minister was forced to resign, such ___ on her.
options: the pressure was / was the pressure

items.prompt: So nervous ___ that I was almost certain he was lying.

exercises.title: F · Cleft sentences
exercises.instruction: Rewrite each sentence, starting with the word(s) given. Write the complete sentence.

items.prompt:
The window was broken by a cricket ball.
**It**
acceptedAnswers: It was a cricket ball that broke the window.
It was a cricket ball which broke the window.
It was a cricket ball that the window was broken by.

items.prompt:
I will never forget the day I heard I'd got into my chosen university.
**The day**
acceptedAnswers: The day I heard I'd got into my chosen university is one I will never forget.
The day I heard I'd got into my chosen university was one I will never forget.
The day I heard I'd got into my chosen university is a day I will never forget.
The day when I heard I'd got into my chosen university is one I will never forget.

items.prompt:
Glynn became a social worker to help people less fortunate than himself.
**The reason**
acceptedAnswers: The reason Glynn became a social worker was to help people less fortunate than himself.
The reason why Glynn became a social worker was to help people less fortunate than himself.

items.prompt:
Getting through the summer without getting injured was the only thing the athlete wanted.
**All**
acceptedAnswers: All the athlete wanted was to get through the summer without getting injured.
All that the athlete wanted was to get through the summer without getting injured.
All the athlete wanted was getting through the summer without getting injured.

items.prompt:
The driver didn't see the motorcyclist.
**What happened**
acceptedAnswers: What happened was that the driver didn't see the motorcyclist.
What happened was the driver didn't see the motorcyclist.

items.prompt:
Christopher Columbus discovered America.
**The person**
acceptedAnswers: The person who discovered America was Christopher Columbus.
The person that discovered America was Christopher Columbus.

items.prompt:
Seeing Patricia cry like that made me feel guilty.
**What**
acceptedAnswers: What made me feel guilty was seeing Patricia cry like that.
What made me feel guilty was to see Patricia cry like that.

items.prompt:
What we had to do first was decide where to meet.
**The first thing**
acceptedAnswers: The first thing we had to do was decide where to meet.
The first thing that we had to do was decide where to meet.
The first thing we had to do was to decide where to meet.

items.prompt:
There are lots of facilities where we go camping.
**The place**
acceptedAnswers: The place where we go camping has lots of facilities.
The place where we go camping is one with lots of facilities.
The place where we go camping has a lot of facilities.

items.prompt:
Einstein proved that energy and mass are basically the same thing.
**What**
acceptedAnswers: What Einstein proved was that energy and mass are basically the same thing.
What Einstein did was prove that energy and mass are basically the same thing.
